literature.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 研究发现,TRPV4介导的钙离子内流在37°C条件下促进了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的有效复制,且环孢素A与马尼地平均可抑制病毒复制,并保护叙利亚仓鼠免受Delta变异株致死性感染。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014520]
VLP免疫小鼠的血清能够有效中和同源武汉系毒株,但对JN.1变异株则未表现出可检测的中和活性。 [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129059]
本综述识别出十三个美国严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、流感与RSV监测数据源。研究强调多数系统为基于病例的系统,部分采用综合性或非常规方法(如废水监测)。这些系统收集的数据对公共卫生干预至关重要。 [10.1007/s40471-026-00405-w]
部分抗体组别可介导进入THP1来源巨噬细胞,而其他组别则无此能力;此类入侵可被其他组别的抗体抑制。 [10.1128/spectrum.00120-26]
单细胞RNA测序显示出显著的上皮重塑,包括纤毛细胞丢失、干扰素应答受抑以及部分上皮-间充质转化启动。内皮细胞血管生成反应表现为扩增的血管生成尖端样状态及血管内皮生长因子(VEGF)非依赖性血管生成配体程序,且上述反应在四种变异株中保持一致。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10547160/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: COVID-19 vaccines were effective in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation and death in this population, but vaccine effectiveness waned over time and during the post-Omicron variant period. [10.1080/22423982.2026.2706888]

The study found that TRPV4-mediated calcium influx contributes to efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication at 37°C, and both cyclosporine A and manidipine suppressed viral replication and protected Syrian hamsters from lethal infection with the Delta variant. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014520]
Sera from VLP-immunized mice efficiently neutralized the homologous Wuhan-lineage strain but showed no detectable neutralizing activity against the JN.1 variant. [10.1016/j.vaccine.2026.129059]

The review identifies thirteen surveillance data sources for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV in the U.S. It highlights that most systems are case-based, with some using syndromic or non-traditional methods like wastewater surveillance. The data collected by these systems are essential for public health interventions. [10.1007/s40471-026-00405-w]
Some antibody groups mediated entry into THP1-derived macrophages, while others did not, and entry was inhibitable by antibodies from other groups. [10.1128/spectrum.00120-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

COVID-19 vaccines were effective in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation and death in this population, but vaccine effectiveness waned over time and during the post-Omicron variant period.

papers.title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
papers.abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in 70.2% (33/47) of immunocompromised patients with mAb-resistant infections, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term outcomes, durability of viral clearance, or comparative efficacy against newer antiviral agents. Additionally, the small sample size (47 cases) and reliance on unpublished cases limit generalizability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for randomized controlled trials to validate CCP efficacy in immunocompromised populations and to determine optimal dosing strategies. Surveillance for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants resistant to both mAbs and CCP is recommended to guide treatment protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes correlating with improved outcomes. The review underscores CCP's potential role in overcoming mAb resistance but emphasizes the need for larger, controlled studies to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and assess long-term durability. Given the limited sample size and reliance on unpublished data, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进行随机对照试验来验证 CCP 在免疫功能低下人群中的疗效并确定最佳剂量策略。建议将 监测 用于对 mAb 和 CCP 均具有抗性的新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体,以指导 治疗 方案。

papers.title: Wuhan-ancestral multi-antigen SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particles protect against the omicron sublineage JN.1 variant
papers.abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations in the spike (S) protein, leading to antigenically divergent variants such as the Omicron sublineage JN.1 that markedly reduce vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody activity. These limitations highlight the need for vaccine strategies that can induce multilayered protective immunity rather than relying solely on S protein-targeted immunity. Here, we developed a Wuhan-lineage-based multi-antigen virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine incorporating S, envelope (E), membrane (M), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins using a baculovirus dual-expression system. Mice were primed intramuscularly and boosted via either the intramuscular or intranasal route, and humoral, mucosal, and cellular immune responses were evaluated. Both vaccination regimens induced robust systemic IgG responses, whereas mucosal IgA responses were selectively enhanced following intranasal boosting. Sera from VLP-immunized mice efficiently neutralized the homologous Wuhan-lineage strain but showed no detectable neutralizing activity against the JN.1 variant. Despite this, VLP immunization elicited antigen-specific CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both pulmonary and systemic compartments. In a highly susceptible K18-hACE2 mouse model, VLP immunization completely prevented mortality following challenge with both the ancestral Wuhan-lineage strain and the JN.1 variant and markedly suppressed viral replication in respiratory tissues. Histopathological analysis further showed minimal interstitial lung lesions with organized perivascular lymphocytic infiltration in vaccinated mice, while pulmonary cytokine analysis revealed qualitatively distinct immune response patterns depending on the challenge strain and vaccination status. Our findings show that a Wuhan-lineage-based multi-antigen VLP vaccine can provide cross-protection against an antigenically divergent SARS-CoV-2 variant that is not fully explained by detectable serum neutralizing activity alone, suggesting the importance of integrated immune responses involving humoral, cellular, and local immune mechanisms.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the protective efficacy of a Wuhan-ancestral multi-antigen SARS-CoV-2 virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine against the Omicron sublineage JN.1 variant. The research is motivated by the antigenic divergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly JN.1, which reduces vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody activity. The study design involves developing a multi-antigen VLP vaccine and testing its immunogenicity and protective capacity in mice. The methods include the use of a baculovirus dual-expression system to produce the vaccine and evaluating humoral, mucosal, and cellular immune responses. The main results show that sera from VLP-immunized mice neutralized the homologous Wuhan-lineage strain but not the JN.1 variant. However, the vaccine elicited strong CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in both pulmonary and systemic compartments. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that cross-protection against antigenically divergent variants like JN.1 may involve integrated immune responses beyond neutralizing antibodies. The scientific and public health significance lies in the potential for multi-antigen vaccines to offer broader protection against emerging variants. The study's limitations include the reliance on a mouse model and the absence of direct neutralizing activity against JN.1, but the evidence is considered strong due to the comprehensive immune response evaluation.

papers.title_zh: 武汉祖传多抗原严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2病毒样颗粒可预防omicron亚谱系JN.1变种
papers.source_body_en: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations in the spike (S) protein, leading to antigenically divergent variants such as the Omicron sublineage JN.1 that markedly reduce vaccine-induced neutralizing antibody activity. These limitations highlight the need for vaccine strategies that can induce multilayered protective immunity rather than relying solely on S protein-targeted immunity. Here, we developed a Wuhan-lineage-based multi-antigen virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine incorporating S, envelope (E), membrane (M), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins using a baculovirus dual-expression system. Mice were primed intramuscularly and boosted via either the intramuscular or intranasal route, and humoral, mucosal, and cellular immune responses were evaluated. Both vaccination regimens induced robust systemic IgG responses, whereas mucosal IgA responses were selectively enhanced following intranasal boosting. Sera from VLP-immunized mice efficiently neutralized the homologous Wuhan-lineage strain but showed no detectable neutralizing activity against the JN.1 variant. Despite this, VLP immunization elicited antigen-specific CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both pulmonary and systemic compartments. In a highly susceptible K18-hACE2 mouse model, VLP immunization completely prevented mortality following challenge with both the ancestral Wuhan-lineage strain and the JN.1 variant and markedly suppressed viral replication in respiratory tissues. Histopathological analysis further showed minimal interstitial lung lesions with organized perivascular lymphocytic infiltration in vaccinated mice, while pulmonary cytokine analysis revealed qualitatively distinct immune response patterns depending on the challenge strain and vaccination status. Our findings show that a Wuhan-lineage-based multi-antigen VLP vaccine can provide cross-protection against an antigenically divergent SARS-CoV-2 variant that is not fully explained by detectable serum neutralizing activity alone, suggesting the importance of integrated immune responses involving humoral, cellular, and local immune mechanisms.
papers.abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)通过刺突蛋白(S)蛋白的突变持续进化,导致抗原性差异的变异株,如奥密克戎亚系JN.1,显著降低抗病毒药物诱导的中和抗体活性。这些局限性凸显了开发能够诱导多层保护性免疫而非仅依赖S蛋白靶向免疫的抗病毒药物策略的必要性。在此,我们利用杆状病毒双表达系统开发了一种基于武汉系的多抗原病毒样颗粒(VLP)疫苗,该疫苗整合了S、包膜(E)、膜(M)和核衣壳(N)蛋白。小鼠通过肌肉注射进行初次免疫,并通过肌肉注射或鼻腔途径进行加强免疫,评估了体液、黏膜和细胞免疫应答。两种加强方案均诱导了强效的全身IgG反应,而通过鼻腔加强则特异性增强了黏膜IgA反应。VLP免疫小鼠的血清能够有效中和同源武汉系毒株,但对JN.1变异株则未表现出可检测的中和活性。尽管如此,VLP免疫在肺部和全身均诱导了抗原特异性的CD4+和CD8+ T细胞反应。在高度易感的K18-hACE2小鼠模型中,VLP免疫完全防止了病毒在武汉系毒株和JN.1变异株挑战后的感染,并显著抑制了呼吸道组织中的病毒复制。组织病理学分析进一步显示,接种VLP的小鼠肺部仅有轻微的间质性肺病变,并伴有组织化的血管周围淋巴细胞浸润。肺部细胞因子分析还揭示了根据挑战毒株和免疫状态而定的免疫应答模式差异。我们的研究结果表明,基于武汉系的多抗原VLP疫苗能够提供对抗原性差异的变异株的交叉保护,这种保护不能仅通过可检测的血清中和活性来完全解释,提示了整合体液、细胞和局部免疫机制的重要性。

papers.title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
papers.abstract: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) for COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2, focusing on three interacting determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics, to reconcile conflicting trial outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM) was conducted, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through May 2026, applying a standardized 91-field extraction matrix to 31 included studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CP is effective only under specific conditions: early administration, sufficient antibody titre, and in seronegative or immunocompromised hosts lacking endogenous antibody responses. Among RCTs, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration, 3 of 4 with higher-titre CP, and two large RCTs (n=12,522) showed preferential benefit in seronegative recipients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM) in CP products is nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies reporting such data despite evidence of their potent neutralising activity against SARS-CoV-2, representing a systematic gap in product assessment.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritise standardised quantification of IgA/IgM titres in CP products and evaluate precision deployment strategies for passive immunotherapy in future pandemics, leveraging timing and titre determinants to optimise efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review resolves conflicting evidence on convalescent plasma (CP) efficacy in COVID-19 by identifying three critical determinants: early administration, high antibody titre, and host seronegativity or immunocompromise. Among 31 studies (20,793 patients), randomized trials showed benefit when CP was given early (4/6 trials) or with higher titres (3/4 trials), particularly in seronegative recipients (two large RCTs, n=12,522). However, a major evidence gap persists: only 2 studies assessed non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM), despite their potential potency. The review reframes CP efficacy as conditional and provides a template for precision deployment in future pandemics, emphasizing the need for standardized IgA/IgM quantification and targeted clinical strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) for COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2, focusing on three interacting determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics, to reconcile conflicting trial outcomes.
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 进行了设计分层叙述综合的系统评价(PRISMA 2020;SWiM),检索 PubMed、Web of Science 和 Scopus,直至 2026 年 5 月,将标准化的 91 场提取矩阵应用于 31 项纳入研究(20,793 名患者;8 项随机对照试验,23 项观察性研究)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CP 仅在特定条件下有效:早期给药、足够的抗体滴度以及缺乏内源性抗体反应的血清阴性或免疫功能低下的 宿主。在随机对照试验中,6 项中的 4 项发现早期给药有益,4 项中的 3 项发现较高滴度的 CP 有益,两项大型随机对照试验 (n=12,522) 显示对血清阴性受者有优先益处。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: CP 产品中的非 IgG 免疫球蛋白 (IgA/IgM) 的表征几乎不存在,尽管有证据表明它们对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 具有有效的中和活性,但 31 项研究中只有 2 项报告了此类数据,这代表了产品评估中的系统性差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先考虑 CP 产品中 IgA/IgM 滴度的标准化量化,并评估未来大流行中被动免疫治疗的精确部署策略,利用时机和滴度决定因素来优化疗效。

papers.title: Mapping the Surveillance Data Infrastructure in the U.S. for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
papers.abstract: Infectious disease surveillance forms the epidemiological bedrock of public health, supporting the continuous and systematic collection, and analysis of health data. However, these data are collected by a fragmented network of systems and entities which complicate their accessibility and efficient use. This review describes the key surveillance systems tracking three important respiratory viruses: influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2; highlights these systems' limitations; and identifies opportunities for improvement. High quality surveillance data are vital for effective public health interventions. The decentralized nature of the U.S. public health infrastructure and the subsequent patchwork of surveillance networks create a formidable challenge for epidemiologists seeking to mobilize these data for outbreak response, policy evaluation, or population-based research. Greater clarity on these key surveillance systems, the data they collect, and the populations they represent could support their more effective use to support public health research and emergency response. We identified thirteen surveillance data sources monitoring influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in the U.S; all but one were governmental. Most (9) were case-based systems, 2 were syndromic surveillance systems (that monitor for increases in illness-associated symptoms in a population rather than the disease itself), and 2 were classified as "non-traditional" sources like wastewater surveillance systems. We also assessed the relative accessibility of data from these systems and of data from state and local entities which often feed into these systems, and collated this information to improve its findability and accessibility. The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40471-026-00405-w.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies thirteen surveillance data sources for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV in the U.S. It highlights that most systems are case-based, with some using syndromic or non-traditional methods like wastewater surveillance. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The decentralized nature of the U.S. public health infrastructure and the patchwork of surveillance networks create challenges for epidemiologists. There is a lack of clarity on the data collected by these systems and the populations they represent, which hinders their effective use for outbreak response and population-based research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Greater clarity on the key surveillance systems, the data they collect, and the populations they represent could support their more effective use for public health research and emergency response. analysis.summary_en: This review maps the surveillance data infrastructure in the U.S. for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV, highlighting the fragmented nature of these systems and their limitations. The review underscores the importance of high-quality surveillance data for public health interventions and calls for greater clarity and accessibility of these systems to enhance their utility in outbreak response and research.

papers.abstract_zh: 传染病监测构成公共卫生的流行病学基石,支撑健康数据的持续系统性收集与分析。然而,这些数据由碎片化的系统与实体网络收集,其可及性与高效利用受到复杂化影响。本综述描述了三种重要呼吸道病毒——流感、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2——的关键监测系统,突出这些系统的局限性,并识别改进机遇。高质量监测数据对有效公共卫生干预至关重要。美国公共卫生基础设施的分散性及由此形成的监测网络补丁式拼接,为试图动员这些数据用于疫情应对、政策评估或基于人群的研究的流行病学家带来了严峻挑战。明确这些关键监测系统、其收集的数据及所代表的人群,可支持其更有效地用于公共卫生研究与应急响应。我们识别出十三个在美国监测流感、RSV与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的监测数据源;除一个外均为政府系统。其中多数(9个)为基于病例的系统,2个为综合性监测系统(监测人群中与疾病相关症状增加而非疾病本身),2个被归类为“非常规”数据源,如废水监测系统。我们还评估了这些系统及常向其提供数据的州与地方实体的数据相对可及性,并汇编信息以提升其可发现性与可及性。在线版本包含补充材料,可于10.1007/s40471-026-00405-w访问。

papers.title: TRPV4-mediated calcium influx contributes temperature-dependent SARS-CoV-2 replication
papers.abstract: Temperature varies across the nasal cavity, lower respiratory tract, and during febrile conditions, yet the impact of these differences on SARS-CoV-2 replication remains poorly understood. Here, we show that ancestral SARS-CoV-2, Delta, or Omicron BA.5 variants replicate most efficiently at 37°C. We found that transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4)-mediated calcium influx, a thermosensitive cation channel known to be activated at 37°C, contributes to efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication. In addition, a calcineurin inhibitor, cyclosporine A (Cys A), and manidipine, an FDA-approved calcium channel blocker, both suppressed viral replication and protected Syrian hamsters from lethal infection with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. Notably, a selective TRPV4 antagonist also conferred protection in infected hamsters. These results suggest that TRPV4-mediated calcium influx contributes to efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication at 37°C and highlight manidipine as a strong candidate for repurposing as an anti-SARS-CoV-2 therapeutic.

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the temperature-dependent mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 replication and suggest a possible therapeutic strategy for targeting viral replication in humans.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to animal models and does not include human clinical data, but the evidence is strong due to the direct link between TRPV4 activity and viral replication in a controlled setting.

papers.title_zh: TRPV4介导的钙离子内流促进了温度依赖性严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制
papers.source_body_en: Temperature varies across the nasal cavity, lower respiratory tract, and during febrile conditions, yet the impact of these differences on SARS-CoV-2 replication remains poorly understood. Here, we show that ancestral SARS-CoV-2, Delta, or Omicron BA.5 variants replicate most efficiently at 37°C. We found that transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4)-mediated calcium influx, a thermosensitive cation channel known to be activated at 37°C, contributes to efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication. In addition, a calcineurin inhibitor, cyclosporine A (Cys A), and manidipine, an FDA-approved calcium channel blocker, both suppressed viral replication and protected Syrian hamsters from lethal infection with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. Notably, a selective TRPV4 antagonist also conferred protection in infected hamsters. These results suggest that TRPV4-mediated calcium influx contributes to efficient SARS-CoV-2 replication at 37°C and highlight manidipine as a strong candidate for repurposing as an anti-SARS-CoV-2 therapeutic.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探究鼻腔、下呼吸道及发热状态下的温度差异如何影响严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制,因这些差异的影响尚未得到充分理解。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究表明,祖系严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、Delta或Omicron BA.5变异株在37°C条件下复制效率最高,并以叙利亚仓鼠作为感染模型。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员确定TRPV4介导的钙离子内流是一种在37°C被激活的热敏阳离子通道,并通过钙调磷酸酶抑制剂环孢素A(Cys A)及FDA批准的钙通道阻滞剂马尼地平,测试其在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制中的作用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,TRPV4介导的钙离子内流在37°C条件下促进了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的有效复制,且环孢素A与马尼地平均可抑制病毒复制,并保护叙利亚仓鼠免受Delta变异株致死性感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,TRPV4介导的钙离子内流是严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2在体温下复制的关键因素,并凸显马尼地平作为潜在治疗药物再利用的可能性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为理解严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2复制的温度依赖性机制提供了见解,并为靶向人类病毒复制的潜在治疗策略提供了可能。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于动物模型,未纳入人体临床数据,但由于在受控环境中直接关联TRPV4活性与病毒复制,证据较为充分。

papers.title: Effectiveness of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) original vaccines to prevent COVID-19-related hospitalisations among Alaska Native peoples, January 2021–October 2022
papers.abstract: American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) peoples experienced some of the highest rates of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) disease in the United States. However, there are limited data on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in this population. We performed a test-negative case‒control study using electronic health record data to evaluate the effectiveness of the original three FDA-authorised vaccines to prevent COVID-19-associated hospitalisations among AI/AN adults during 2021-2022. COVID-19 vaccines were effective in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation and death in this population. However, vaccine effectiveness waned over time and during the post-Omicron variant time period. Booster vaccination proved effective during a period when the Omicron variant was circulating. Waning effectiveness with time and the introduction of new variants supports the need to stay up-to-date with SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Evaluating vaccine effectiveness using electronic health records proved to be a useful tool during a pandemic.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A test-negative case–control study was conducted using electronic health record data to evaluate the effectiveness of the original three FDA-authorised COVID-19 vaccines in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisations among Alaska Native adults during January 2021 to October 2022.
analysis.methods: The study used electronic health records in a test-negative case–control design to assess vaccine effectiveness against COVID-19-associated hospitalisations, intensive care unit admissions, mechanical ventilation and death.
analysis.main_results: COVID-19 vaccines were effective in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation and death in this population, but vaccine effectiveness waned over time and during the post-Omicron variant period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating that booster vaccination remained effective during Omicron circulation, highlighting the need to stay up-to-date with SARS-CoV-2 vaccination as effectiveness wanes with time and new variants emerge.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study supports the use of electronic health records for rapid vaccine effectiveness evaluation during pandemics and underscores the importance of booster doses to maintain protection against severe outcomes in high-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s reliance on electronic health records may introduce data completeness and selection biases, and the observational design limits causal inference; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of original COVID-19 vaccines in preventing severe outcomes among Alaska Native adults using a test-negative case–control design with electronic health records from January 2021 to October 2022. Vaccines were effective against hospitalisation, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation and death, but protection waned over time and during the Omicron period. Booster doses remained effective during Omicron circulation, supporting the need for updated vaccination to sustain immunity. The study demonstrates the utility of electronic health records for real-time vaccine effectiveness assessment but is limited by potential biases and an observational design, warranting moderate confidence in the findings.

papers.title_zh: Effectiveness of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) original vaccines to prevent COVID-19-related hospitalisations among Alaska Native peoples, January 2021–October 2022
papers.source_body_en: American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) peoples experienced some of the highest rates of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) disease in the United States. However, there are limited data on COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in this population. We performed a test-negative case‒control study using electronic health record data to evaluate the effectiveness of the original three FDA-authorised vaccines to prevent COVID-19-associated hospitalisations among AI/AN adults during 2021-2022. COVID-19 vaccines were effective in preventing COVID-19-associated hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation and death in this population. However, vaccine effectiveness waned over time and during the post-Omicron variant time period. Booster vaccination proved effective during a period when the Omicron variant was circulating. Waning effectiveness with time and the introduction of new variants supports the need to stay up-to-date with SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Evaluating vaccine effectiveness using electronic health records proved to be a useful tool during a pandemic.

papers.title: Association between psychological wellbeing and the COVID-19-related outcomes in Europeans aged ≥ 50 years old: The SHARE study.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The aim of the present study was to prospectively investigate the associations between psychological wellbeing and COVID-19 outcomes (vaccination, infection, long COVID) based on the Survey of Health, Aging, and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), using the data from Wave 8 and two supplementary COVID-19 surveys (Corona Survey 1 and 2) covering 27 European countries and Israel. Furthermore, we also conducted a cross-sectional study to evaluated the joint effects of wellbeing and vaccination status on the risks of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID. A total of 29,597 participants were included in this study. Psychological wellbeing was measured using the Control, Autonomy, Self-realization, and Pleasure (CASP)-12 scale. Multivariable logistic regression models were performed to explore these associations, and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Compared with participants in the lowest CASP-12 score group, those in the highest group had significantly higher odds of COVID-19 vaccination (OR 2.68, 95% CI: 2.44–2.96) and a significant 23% reduction in the likelihood of long COVID (OR 0.77, 95% CI: 0.64–0.93). However, we failed to observe a significant association on infection risk (OR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.74–1.02). Protective effects were more pronounced with higher CASP-12 scores. Higher psychological wellbeing was associated with increased COVID-19 vaccination and reduced risks of infection and long COVID among European adults aged 50 y and older. Further high-quality studies were warranted to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Identification and Masking of Artefactual and Misleading Within-Host Variants in Deep-Sequencing SARS-CoV-2 Data.
papers.abstract: Deep sequencing data are increasingly used to study within-host viral diversity and to inform evolutionary inference. For SARS-CoV-2, analyses based on intra-host single-nucleotide variants (iSNVs) have been widely applied to quantify within-host diversity and infer transmission dynamics. However, these applications critically depend on the reliable identification of low-frequency variants, which remain vulnerable to systematic and technical artefacts. In this study, we show that recurrent artefactual iSNVs are common in large-scale SARS-CoV-2 sequencing data and can persist even under conservative minor allele frequency (MAF) thresholds. Using data from the UK's Office for National Statistics COVID-19 Infection Survey, we demonstrate that such artefacts are predominantly sequencing centre- rather than primer-specific. Each centre exhibits a modest, distinct set of recurrent artefactual variants showing little overlap with sites routinely masked at the consensus level. To address this, we developed a systematic, dataset-aware framework that uses recurrence within sequencing datasets to identify small, noise-adapted sets of artefactual iSNVs to mask. Applying this framework reduces spurious sharing of low-frequency variants between samples and qualitatively alters downstream inferences, including estimates of within-host diversity and transmission bottleneck sizes. Although this study focussed on SARS-CoV-2, it is likely that recurrent artefactual iSNVs will be problematic for other viruses as mass-sequencing becomes increasingly routine. Together, these findings highlight the importance of explicit, dataset-aware artefact control for robust inference from within-host variation, particularly as genomic studies increasingly seek to exploit sub-consensus diversity in rapidly evolving pathogens.

papers.title: Recapitulating SARS-CoV-2 Infection in a Human Lung Organoid-on-a-Chip at the Air-Liquid Interface
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Chronic respiratory diseases and emerging pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2 are a major global health burden. Traditional in vitro models, however, poorly recapitulate the functional complexity of the human lung, limiting mechanistic study and therapeutic development. Methods To address this, we developed a lung organoid-on-a-chip in which patient-derived airway organoids are differentiated at an air–liquid interface and co-cultured with vascular endothelial cells and macrophages on a microfluidic platform. The chip was infected with four SARS-CoV-2 variants - Wuhan, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron XBB.1 - and profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. Results The platform reconstituted native airway cellular composition within an air–liquid interface, and single-cell profiling revealed pronounced epithelial remodeling, including loss of ciliated cells, blunted interferon responses, and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition priming. This was accompanied by an endothelial angiogenic response marked by an expanded angiogenic tip-like state and a VEGF-independent angiogenic-ligand program, with these responses remaining consistent across all four variants. Conclusions Collectively, this lung organoid-on-a-chip recapitulates conserved SARS-CoV-2 epithelial and vascular responses, providing a physiologically relevant platform for respiratory disease research.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a more accurate in vitro model of the human lung to better understand SARS-CoV-2 infection and its effects on respiratory tissues.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the creation of a lung organoid-on-a-chip model using patient-derived airway organoids co-cultured with vascular endothelial cells and macrophages. The model was infected with four SARS-CoV-2 variants: Wuhan, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron XBB.1.
analysis.methods: The lung organoid-on-a-chip was differentiated at an air–liquid interface and infected with four SARS-CoV-2 variants. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to profile the cellular responses to infection.
analysis.main_results: Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed pronounced epithelial remodeling, including loss of ciliated cells, blunted interferon responses, and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition priming. The endothelial angiogenic response was marked by an expanded angiogenic tip-like state and a VEGF-independent angiogenic-ligand program, with these responses remaining consistent across all four variants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating that the lung organoid-on-a-chip model effectively recapitulates conserved SARS-CoV-2 epithelial and vascular responses, offering a physiologically relevant platform for studying respiratory disease mechanisms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a valuable tool for respiratory disease research, enabling more accurate study of SARS-CoV-2 infection and its impact on lung tissues, which could inform future therapeutic development and mechanistic studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro observations and does not account for in vivo complexities. However, the evidence is strong as it directly reports on the platform's ability to recapitulate SARS-CoV-2 responses across multiple variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a lung organoid-on-a-chip model that mimics the human lung environment at the air-liquid interface. The model was infected with four SARS-CoV-2 variants, and single-cell RNA sequencing revealed significant epithelial remodeling and consistent endothelial responses across all variants. These findings suggest the platform's utility in studying SARS-CoV-2 infection mechanisms and could support future research into respiratory disease and therapeutic development. The study's in vitro nature limits its applicability to in vivo conditions, but the results are robust and relevant for understanding the virus's effects on lung tissues.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在构建更精确的人肺体外模型,以更好地理解严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染及其对呼吸组织的影响。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究构建了一种肺类器官芯片模型,采用患者来源的气道类器官与血管内皮细胞和巨噬细胞共培养。该模型被用于感染四种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株:原始株(Wuhan)、Delta、Omicron BA.1及Omicron XBB.1。
elements_zh.methods: 肺类器官芯片在气液界面分化,并感染四种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株。随后通过单细胞RNA测序对感染后的细胞反应进行表征。
elements_zh.main_results: 单细胞RNA测序显示出显著的上皮重塑,包括纤毛细胞丢失、干扰素应答受抑以及部分上皮-间充质转化启动。内皮细胞血管生成反应表现为扩增的血管生成尖端样状态及血管内皮生长因子(VEGF)非依赖性血管生成配体程序,且上述反应在四种变异株中保持一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明肺类器官芯片模型有效重现了保守的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2上皮与血管反应,并提供了一种生理相关的平台用于研究呼吸系统疾病机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该发现为呼吸系统疾病研究提供了有价值的工具,使更精确地研究严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染及其对肺组织的影响成为可能,并有望为未来治疗开发与机制研究提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外观察,未考虑体内复杂性。然而,证据较为充分,因其直接报道了该平台在多种变异株中重现严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2反应的能力。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 慢性呼吸系统疾病及新发病原体(如严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)是全球主要的健康负担。然而,传统体外模型难以重现人肺的功能复杂性,限制了机制研究与治疗开发。方法 为解决这一问题,本研究构建了一种肺类器官芯片,其中患者来源的气道类器官在气液界面分化,并与微流控平台上的血管内皮细胞和巨噬细胞共培养。该芯片被用于感染四种严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株——原始株(Wuhan)、Delta、Omicron BA.1及Omicron XBB.1——并通过单细胞RNA测序进行表征。结果 该平台在气液界面重建了原生气道细胞组成,单细胞表征显示出显著的上皮重塑,包括纤毛细胞丢失、干扰素应答受抑以及部分上皮-间充质转化启动。同时伴随内皮细胞血管生成反应,表现为扩增的血管生成尖端样状态及血管内皮生长因子(VEGF)非依赖性血管生成配体程序,且上述反应在四种变异株中保持一致。结论 综合而言,该肺类器官芯片重现了保守的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2上皮与血管反应,为呼吸系统疾病研究提供了一种生理相关的平台。

papers.title: Familial acute necrotizing encephalopathy temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Rationale: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) is a rare but life-threatening parainfectious encephalopathy characterized by rapid neurological deterioration following viral infections. Although most cases occur sporadically, familial clustering is uncommon and suggests the involvement of genetic susceptibility factors. The emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has broadened the spectrum of viral triggers associated with ANE; however, familial COVID-19–associated ANE remains rarely reported. Patient concerns: We retrospectively reviewed 2 siblings who developed ANE following laboratory-confirmed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection in December 2022. The first patient was an 18-year-old woman who presented with seizures and progressive impairment of consciousness 2 days after COVID-19 infection. Her 24-year-old brother developed a similar neurological syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection, characterized by altered mental status and rapid clinical deterioration. Diagnose: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the female patient demonstrated typical bilateral symmetrical lesions involving the thalami, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, cerebellum, and cerebral white matter. MRI of her brother revealed bilateral symmetrical lesions predominantly affecting the lenticular and caudate nuclei. Genetic analysis showed no pathogenic variants in the RANBP2 gene. After comprehensive exclusion of alternative diagnoses, including other infectious encephalitis, metabolic disorders, autoimmune encephalitis, and toxic encephalopathy, both patients were diagnosed with COVID-19–associated ANE. Interventions: Both patients received immunomodulatory therapy, including high-dose corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin. Supportive treatments and intensive neurological monitoring were also provided according to clinical conditions. Outcomes: Following treatment, both patients achieved partial neurological recovery; however, residual neurological impairment remained during short-term follow-up. The clinical course and neuroimaging findings were consistent with previously reported characteristics of ANE. Lessons: These familial cases highlight a potential association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of ANE and suggest that genetic susceptibility factors other than RANBP2 mutations may contribute to disease pathogenesis. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, prompt brain MRI evaluation, and timely initiation of immunomodulatory therapy may improve clinical outcomes. Further genetic and mechanistic studies are warranted to identify additional susceptibility genes involved in COVID-19–associated ANE.

papers.title_original: Familial acute necrotizing encephalopathy temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on familial acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. The central question is whether SARS-CoV-2 infection can lead to ANE, particularly in familial contexts, and whether genetic susceptibility factors other than RANBP2 mutations may contribute to this association.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report of 2 siblings who developed ANE following laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in December 2022. The authors conducted a retrospective analysis of these cases, excluding alternative diagnoses such as other infectious encephalitis, metabolic disorders, autoimmune encephalitis, and toxic encephalopathy. The study design is observational, with no meta-analysis or pooled estimates reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The clinical course and neuroimaging findings of the 2 patients were consistent with previously reported characteristics of ANE. The cases suggest a potential association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of ANE, and highlight the possibility of genetic susceptibility factors other than RANBP2 mutations contributing to the disease pathogenesis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that familial COVID-19–associated ANE remains rarely reported. There is no genetic analysis confirming the involvement of RANBP2 mutations, and the study does not provide a comprehensive analysis of potential genetic factors. The findings are limited to 2 cases, which may not be sufficient to draw broad conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further genetic and mechanistic studies are needed to identify additional susceptibility genes involved in COVID-19–associated ANE. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, prompt brain MRI evaluation, and timely initiation of immunomodulatory therapy may improve clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes 2 siblings who developed acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) following SARS-CoV-2 infection in December 2022. The clinical and neuroimaging findings were consistent with previously reported ANE characteristics. Genetic analysis ruled out RANBP2 mutations as a cause, suggesting other genetic susceptibility factors may be involved. The cases highlight the need for further research into the genetic and mechanistic basis of ANE associated with SARS-CoV-2. Early recognition and prompt treatment with immunomodulatory therapy are emphasized as potential strategies to improve outcomes.

papers.title_zh: 家族性急性坏死性脑病与严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的时间关联
papers.source_body_en: Rationale: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) is a rare but life-threatening parainfectious encephalopathy characterized by rapid neurological deterioration following viral infections. Although most cases occur sporadically, familial clustering is uncommon and suggests the involvement of genetic susceptibility factors. The emergence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has broadened the spectrum of viral triggers associated with ANE; however, familial COVID-19–associated ANE remains rarely reported. Patient concerns: We retrospectively reviewed 2 siblings who developed ANE following laboratory-confirmed severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection in December 2022. The first patient was an 18-year-old woman who presented with seizures and progressive impairment of consciousness 2 days after COVID-19 infection. Her 24-year-old brother developed a similar neurological syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection, characterized by altered mental status and rapid clinical deterioration. Diagnose: Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the female patient demonstrated typical bilateral symmetrical lesions involving the thalami, basal ganglia, corpus callosum, cerebellum, and cerebral white matter. MRI of her brother revealed bilateral symmetrical lesions predominantly affecting the lenticular and caudate nuclei. Genetic analysis showed no pathogenic variants in the RANBP2 gene. After comprehensive exclusion of alternative diagnoses, including other infectious encephalitis, metabolic disorders, autoimmune encephalitis, and toxic encephalopathy, both patients were diagnosed with COVID-19–associated ANE. Interventions: Both patients received immunomodulatory therapy, including high-dose corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin. Supportive treatments and intensive neurological monitoring were also provided according to clinical conditions. Outcomes: Following treatment, both patients achieved partial neurological recovery; however, residual neurological impairment remained during short-term follow-up. The clinical course and neuroimaging findings were consistent with previously reported characteristics of ANE. Lessons: These familial cases highlight a potential association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of ANE and suggest that genetic susceptibility factors other than RANBP2 mutations may contribute to disease pathogenesis. Early recognition of neurological deterioration, prompt brain MRI evaluation, and timely initiation of immunomodulatory therapy may improve clinical outcomes. Further genetic and mechanistic studies are warranted to identify additional susceptibility genes involved in COVID-19–associated ANE.

papers.title: Missed Nursing Care in Pandemic Crisis of COVID-19: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: High-quality nursing care ensures patient safety. However, missed nursing care (MNC) poses a significant risk. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the dynamic clinical environment negatively impacted nurses and patient care quality. This review examined the most frequently reported elements and contributing factors of MNCs in studies conducted during the pandemic. METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42023460938). A systematic search was conducted across databases including ProQuest, CINAHL, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Scopus, PubMed, PROSPERO, and Cochrane CENTRAL, using Boolean operators based on PICOT-SD criteria from December 2019 to July 2024. Keywords were selected based on Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and previous studies. After reviewing the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 31 quantitative studies from 17 countries were included in the final evaluation. Findings were reported following PRISMA guidelines. RESULTS: During the pandemic, MNC elements were categorized into 5 domains based on the Nursing Intervention Classification (NIC). At the same time, contributing factors were organized into 6 levels based on the MNC model. The most frequently observed MNC elements were identified in the basic physiological domain. The primary contributing factor for MNCs was the demand for patient care, with inadequate staffing being the most reported issue during the pandemic. CONCLUSION: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic revealed that nurses' reluctance to engage in close contact with patients for various reasons led to significant losses in care. High care demands and staffing shortages remain prevalent factors contributing to MNCs, highlighting the need for effective management strategies in future health crises.

papers.title: A human-informed multi-patch T-cell vaccine induces broad CD8+ immunity and protects against SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Abstract The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants has highlighted the need for vaccines that complement Spike-directed immunity by targeting conserved T-cell responses. Here, we developed CoV2-TMEPu, a human-informed multi-patch immunogen integrating conserved and naturally immunodominant regions from structural, accessory and replication-associated SARS-CoV-2 proteins into a single mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine. LNP-CoV2-TMEPu was efficiently expressed in vitro and induced early innate immune activation. Homologous prime-boost immunization elicited robust, durable and polyfunctional CD8+ T-cell responses together with lower-magnitude CD4+ responses. Epitope mapping revealed broad but hierarchically organized multispecific recognition spanning multiple viral proteins and a diversified CD8+ memory phenotype. Vaccination also induced cross-reactive neutralizing activity against antigenically distinct Omicron-derived variants and protected K18-hACE2 mice from a lethal SARS-CoV-2 challenge, reducing disease severity and viral burden. Together, these findings establish human-informed multi-patch immunogen design as a promising strategy for next-generation variant-resilient coronavirus vaccines.

source_records.abstract: Abstract The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants has highlighted the need for vaccines that complement Spike-directed immunity by targeting conserved T-cell responses. Here, we developed CoV2-TMEPu, a human-informed multi-patch immunogen integrating conserved and naturally immunodominant regions from structural, accessory and replication-associated SARS-CoV-2 proteins into a single mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine. LNP-CoV2-TMEPu was efficiently expressed in vitro and induced early innate immune activation. Homologous prime-boost immunization elicited robust, durable and polyfunctional CD8+ T-cell responses together with lower-magnitude CD4+ responses. Epitope mapping revealed broad but hierarchically organized multispecific recognition spanning multiple viral proteins and a diversified CD8+ memory phenotype. Vaccination also induced cross-reactive neutralizing activity against antigenically distinct Omicron-derived variants and protected K18-hACE2 mice from a lethal SARS-CoV-2 challenge, reducing disease severity and viral burden. Together, these findings establish human-informed multi-patch immunogen design as a promising strategy for next-generation variant-resilient coronavirus vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a vaccine that complements Spike-directed immunity by targeting conserved T-cell responses against SARS-CoV-2 variants. The researchers created CoV2-TMEPu, a multi-patch immunogen combining conserved and immunodominant regions from various SARS-CoV-2 proteins into an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccine. The vaccine was shown to be efficiently expressed in vitro and to induce early innate immune activation. Homologous prime-boost immunization generated strong, long-lasting CD8+ T-cell responses, along with weaker CD4+ responses. Epitope mapping demonstrated broad, hierarchical recognition of multiple viral proteins and a diverse CD8+ memory phenotype. The vaccine also elicited cross-reactive neutralizing activity against Omicron-derived variants and protected K18-hACE2 mice from lethal SARS-CoV-2 infection, reducing disease severity and viral load. These findings suggest that human-informed multi-patch immunogen design could be a valuable approach for creating vaccines resilient to future variants. The study provides promising evidence for the vaccine's efficacy but is limited by its use of animal models and the absence of human clinical trial data.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 新型冠状病毒感染变异株的出现凸显了对疫苗的需求,其通过靶向保守的T细胞应答补充刺突蛋白导向的免疫。本研究开发了CoV2-TMEPu,一种人源信息驱动的多区段免疫原,将来自严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2结构蛋白、辅助蛋白和复制相关蛋白的保守且天然免疫显性区域整合为单一mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒(LNP)疫苗。LNP-CoV2-TMEPu在体外高效表达并诱导早期固有免疫激活。同源初免-加强免疫诱导了强效、持久且多功能的CD8+ T细胞应答,同时伴有低强度CD4+应答。表位作图显示跨多种病毒蛋白的广泛但分层组织的多特异性识别及多样化的CD8+记忆表型。疫苗接种还诱导了针对抗原性差异显著的Omicron衍生变异株的交叉反应性中和活性,并保护K18-hACE2小鼠免受致死性新型冠状病毒感染攻击,降低了疾病严重程度和病毒载量。综上,这些发现确立了人源信息驱动的多区段免疫原设计作为下一代变异株韧性冠状病毒疫苗的有前景策略。

papers.title: Risk of Post-acute Symptoms and Conditions After SARS-CoV-2 Compared to Other Respiratory Viral Infections: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Background How post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) differs from post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) caused by other respiratory viruses remains uncertain. Comparing these conditions may clarify whether post-acute symptoms reflect specific consequences of SARS-CoV-2 infection or broader post-viral mechanisms. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies comparing persistent symptoms or conditions in adults after SARS-CoV-2 infection with those following other acute respiratory viral infections. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled risks. Results Among 9,371 records screened, 22 studies were included and 14 contributed to the meta-analysis. Increased risk after SARS-CoV-2 infection was observed for pulmonary embolism, abnormal breathing, fatigue, hemorrhagic stroke, memory loss/brain fog, and palpitations; heart rate abnormalities showed borderline significance. For most other outcomes pooled estimates were not significantly more frequent than in other acute respiratory viral infections. Conclusions Our findings support the concept of PCC as one example within the broader spectrum of PAIS, underscoring the need to recognize these conditions after non-COVID respiratory viral infections and to further investigate shared and pathogen-specific mechanisms.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aims to compare the risk of post-acute symptoms and conditions after SARS-CoV-2 infection with those following other respiratory viral infections, focusing on whether these symptoms reflect specific consequences of SARS-CoV-2 or broader post-viral mechanisms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of cohort studies comparing persistent symptoms or conditions in adults after SARS-CoV-2 infection with those following other acute respiratory viral infections. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched, and random-effects models were used to estimate pooled risks.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with an increased risk of specific post-acute symptoms and conditions, including pulmonary embolism, abnormal breathing, fatigue, hemorrhagic stroke, memory loss/brain fog, and palpitations. Heart rate abnormalities showed borderline significance. For most other outcomes, pooled estimates were not significantly more frequent than in other acute respiratory viral infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges that the evidence for some outcomes, such as heart rate abnormalities, was borderline significant. Additionally, the study highlights the need for further research to distinguish between shared post-viral mechanisms and pathogen-specific effects.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the importance of recognizing post-acute symptoms after non-COVID respiratory viral infections and emphasize the need for further investigation into both shared and pathogen-specific mechanisms. This could inform future research, surveillance, and clinical management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis compare the risk of post-acute symptoms and conditions after SARS-CoV-2 infection with those following other respiratory viral infections. The study included 22 cohort studies, with 14 contributing to the meta-analysis. Results showed increased risks for specific conditions such as pulmonary embolism, fatigue, and brain fog after SARS-CoV-2 infection, while most other outcomes did not show significant differences. The review supports the concept of post-COVID condition as part of a broader spectrum of post-viral syndromes and highlights the need for further research to understand shared and pathogen-specific mechanisms. It also underscores the importance of recognizing these conditions after non-COVID respiratory viral infections.

papers.title: Post-Acute Sequelae of Non-COVID-19 Respiratory Viral Infections: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral infections (RVIs) affect millions annually, yet long-term consequences outside COVID-19 are poorly defined. Post-acute sequelae, encompassing persistent or new physical, cognitive, and mental health impairments, are increasingly recognised as clinically important. We systematically reviewed evidence on post-acute outcomes in adults following non-COVID RVIs to characterise pathogen-specific patterns and highlight areas for future research. Major databases were searched from January 2004 to August 2025 for observational studies reporting symptoms, functional impairment, or new diagnoses ≥ 4 weeks after RVIs. Study characteristics, pathogens, follow-up duration, and organ-specific outcomes were extracted. Risk of bias was evaluated using ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was determined with the GRADE approach. Narrative synthesis was performed owing to heterogeneity. Thirteen studies (n = 631,863) met eligibility criteria. Influenza was the most studied pathogen and consistently associated with long-term pulmonary dysfunction, reduced diffusion capacity, dyspnoea, fatigue, and poorer quality of life. Large cohorts corroborated substantial pulmonary morbidity and less frequent cardiovascular and neuropsychiatric burdens. Two RSV cohorts (n = 1553 and n = 471) showed a predominance of cardiovascular sequelae; respiratory and neurological outcomes were less frequent. A single HMPV cohort (n = 92) reported persistent symptoms in 55% of adults at 90-270 days, most commonly dyspnoea, fatigue, and cough. Overall, the available evidence suggests that non-COVID RVIs are associated with post-acute multi-organ sequelae, particularly following severe infection. Nevertheless, evidence remains fragmented due to inconsistent study designs, limited pathogen coverage, and low certainty. Standardised, prospective, pathogen-specific studies are required to refine these preliminary signals and inform clinical follow-up and prevention strategies.

papers.title: Gut microbiome signatures during acute infection are associated with long COVID.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease. OBJECTIVES: To determine whether the gut microbiome composition in the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection predicts subsequent LC and to investigate the role of microbiome signatures in disease subphenotypes. DESIGN: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study involving 799 outpatient participants tested for SARS-CoV-2 due to similar symptom presentation, including 380 SARS-CoV-2 positive and 419 negative individuals. Stool samples were collected at two time points for metagenomic sequencing. Logistic regression with L1 regularization was employed to predict LC based on the microbiome and clinical metadata. RESULTS: The individuals who developed LC harbored a distinct gut microbiome during acute infection compared to those who recovered fully and uninfected controls with similar symptomatology. However, the temporal changes in the gut microbiome between the acute (0-1 month) and post-acute (1-2 months) phases were similar across the three cohorts. Using machine learning, we showed that the gut microbiome carried a modest signal for subsequent LC, but model performance was insufficient for clinical prediction, likely reflecting the heterogeneous nature of LC. Finally, we identified four LC symptom clusters, with gastrointestinal and fatigue-only groups strongly linked to gut microbiome alterations. CONCLUSION: The gut microbiome can potentially offer solutions for understanding the heterogeneous nature of LC. Larger cohorts and phenotype-aware computational algorithms may help overcome current model performance limitations and support the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether gut microbiome composition during the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection predicts the development of long COVID (LC). It reports that individuals who developed LC had a distinct gut microbiome compared to those who recovered fully and uninfected controls with similar symptoms. These findings highlight the need for larger cohorts and more advanced computational methods to improve understanding and develop targeted strategies for LC.

papers.title_zh: 急性感染期肠道微生物组特征与长新冠相关
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease. OBJECTIVES: To determine whether the gut microbiome composition in the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection predicts subsequent LC and to investigate the role of microbiome signatures in disease subphenotypes. DESIGN: We conducted a longitudinal cohort study involving 799 outpatient participants tested for SARS-CoV-2 due to similar symptom presentation, including 380 SARS-CoV-2 positive and 419 negative individuals. Stool samples were collected at two time points for metagenomic sequencing. Logistic regression with L1 regularization was employed to predict LC based on the microbiome and clinical metadata. RESULTS: The individuals who developed LC harbored a distinct gut microbiome during acute infection compared to those who recovered fully and uninfected controls with similar symptomatology. However, the temporal changes in the gut microbiome between the acute (0-1 month) and post-acute (1-2 months) phases were similar across the three cohorts. Using machine learning, we showed that the gut microbiome carried a modest signal for subsequent LC, but model performance was insufficient for clinical prediction, likely reflecting the heterogeneous nature of LC. Finally, we identified four LC symptom clusters, with gastrointestinal and fatigue-only groups strongly linked to gut microbiome alterations. CONCLUSION: The gut microbiome can potentially offer solutions for understanding the heterogeneous nature of LC. Larger cohorts and phenotype-aware computational algorithms may help overcome current model performance limitations and support the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:新型冠状病毒感染后,10%-30%的非住院患者会出现长新冠(LC)表现,导致显著发病率。急性感染期肠道微生物组组成在长新冠发展中的预测作用尚不明确,部分原因在于该疾病的异质性。目的:确定急性期新型冠状病毒感染感染者的肠道微生物组组成是否可预测后续长新冠,并探索微生物组特征在疾病亚表型中的作用。设计:我们开展了一项纵向队列研究,纳入799名因类似症状表现而接受新型冠状病毒感染检测的门诊患者,其中380名新型冠状病毒感染阳性者和419名阴性者。通过宏基因组测序收集两个时间点的粪便样本。采用L1正则化逻辑回归基于微生物组和临床元数据预测长新冠。结果:与完全康复者及症状相似的未感染对照组相比,发展为长新冠的个体在急性感染期拥有截然不同的肠道微生物组。然而,急性期(0-1个月)与亚急性期(1-2个月)之间的肠道微生物组时间变化在三组中相似。通过机器学习,我们证明肠道微生物组对后续长新冠具有一定预测信号,但模型性能不足以用于临床预测,这可能反映了长新冠的异质性。最后,我们识别出四个长新冠症状簇,其中胃肠道症状和仅疲劳症状组与肠道微生物组改变高度相关。结论:肠道微生物组有望为理解长新冠的异质性提供解决方案。更大规模的纵向队列研究及表型感知计算算法可能有助于克服当前模型性能限制,并支持靶向诊断和治疗策略的开发。

papers.title: Recent Advances in the Design of Inhibitors Targeting the Viral Entry and Replication of the SARS-CoV-2 Virus, Driven by In Silico Approaches
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic has significantly impacted global health, politics, medicine, finance, and society. Since 2020, various mutations have been reported, leading to drug resistance in current treatments against different SARS-CoV-2 strains and a drastic increase in cases of long-COVID. This situation underscores the urgent need to develop targeted and effective drugs to combat the spread of SARS-CoV-2 strains and their mutants, manage long-COVID symptoms and prepare for future pandemics. Currently, the treatment of SARS-CoV-2 focuses on targeting the virus’s entry and replication mechanisms to disrupt its life cycle. This review examines approved drugs, clinical candidates, and inhibitors under development, along with their bioassay data, while highlighting associated challenges. It illustrates how inhibitors bind to active sites, providing insights and emphasizing the importance of in silico studies, such as molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, FEP+, WaterMap, and quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) analyses, and their correlation with experimental studies in expediting the drug discovery process. The review aims to provide researchers with insights into the gaps that need to be addressed concerning mutations affecting viral entry and to prepare for future pandemics.

Since 2020, various mutations have been reported, leading to drug resistance in current treatments against different SARS-CoV-2 strains and a drastic increase in cases of long-COVID. papers.abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2疫情对全球健康、政治、医学、金融及社会产生了重大影响。自2020年以来,已报告多种突变,导致现有治疗对不同严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株产生耐药性,且长新冠病例激增。这一局势凸显了开发针对性强且有效药物以遏制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2株及其突变株传播、管理长新冠症状并应对未来大流行的紧迫需求。目前,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的治疗策略主要聚焦于靶向病毒入侵与复制机制,以干扰其生命周期。本综述检视了已获批药物、临床候选药物及研发中的抑制剂,并结合其生物测定数据,同时强调相关挑战。文中阐述了抑制剂与活性位点结合的机制,为研究者提供见解,并强调计算机模拟研究(如分子对接、分子动力学模拟、FEP+、WaterMap及定量构效关系(QSAR)分析)与实验研究的相关性,从而加速药物发现进程。本综述旨在为研究者提供关于亟待解决的突变影响病毒入侵的差距见解,并为未来大流行做好准备。

papers.title: Inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection for people with severe mental illness during and following vaccination roll-out in England: a retrospective, whole-country linked cohort study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: People with severe mental illness (SMI) had a higher risk of death following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with people without SMI during the COVID-19 pandemic peak. It is unclear whether this risk reduced in later stages after vaccination roll-out. We aimed to assess all-cause and cause-specific mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection in people with or without SMI across pandemic stages, using whole-country data, while accounting for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. METHODS: In this retrospective, whole-country cohort study, we analysed linked electronic health records for all people in England registered to primary care who were alive in November, 2019 (>99% of the population). The study population included people who had COVID-19 between Jan 31, 2020, and June 30, 2023, with information on deaths and vaccination. Data extracted from the NHS England Secure Data Environment provided through the British Heart Foundation Data Science Centre CVD-COVID-UK-COVID-IMPACT Consortium linked datasets were curated to form a dataset in July, 2024. Cox regression estimated differences in all-cause and COVID-19 mortality. Analyses were stratified by pandemic stages, defined by WHO policy and UK Government vaccination roll-out: Jan 31-Sept 30, 2020 (stage 1); Oct 1, 2020-July 18, 2021 (stage 2, vaccination roll-out); and July 19, 2021-June 30, 2023 (stage 3, post-vaccination roll-out). SMI comprised schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or other affective and non-affective disorder with psychosis. A patient and public involvement panel was consulted during design phases of the study. FINDINGS: 13 463 945 people with COVID-19 were identified, of whom 160 190 (1·19%) had SMI. People with SMI were older [mean age [SD], SMI 49·7 years [17·9], non-SMI 45·0 years [17·6]), had a similar sex split (females SMI vs non-SMI: 56·3% vs 56·6%); and were mostly White British (77·3% or 76·3%). People with SMI had higher all-cause mortality than those without (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1·56, 95% CI 1·53-1·59). All-cause mortality risk in people with SMI was elevated in stage 1 (aHR 1·27, 95% CI 1·22-1·32), but larger in the stage 2 (aHR 1·56, 1·51-1·61) and stage 3 (aHR 1·55, 1·50-1·59). Vaccination prevalence was initially higher for people with SMI (in stage 2: 112 795 [73·2%, 95% CI 72·9-73·4], compared with people without SMI, 8 852 970 [67·4%, 67·3-67·4]). By study end, fewer people with SMI were fully vaccinated (127 145 [79·4%, 79·2-79·6]), compared with people without SMI (11 605 915 [87·2%, 87·2-87·3]. Higher COVID-19 mortality risk in people with SMI persisted but was partially attenuated by vaccination (aHR 1·25, 1·17-1·34). INTERPRETATION: Excess mortality in people with SMI persisted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Preventive public health and clinical strategies are needed to address excess mortality and lower vaccination. FUNDING: Health Foundation-Academy of Medical Sciences.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection among people with severe mental illness (SMI) during and after vaccination roll-out in England. Using whole-country linked electronic health records, the researchers found that people with SMI had higher all-cause mortality compared to those without SMI, with the risk being elevated in all pandemic stages. The risk was partially reduced by vaccination, but excess mortality persisted. The study highlights the need for targeted public health and clinical strategies to address the higher mortality risk in people with SMI. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and potential for unmeasured confounding.

papers.title_zh: 英格兰在和后续疫苗接种推广期间,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染后患有严重精神疾病人群的死亡率不平等:一项回顾性全国范围关联队列研究研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: People with severe mental illness (SMI) had a higher risk of death following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with people without SMI during the COVID-19 pandemic peak. It is unclear whether this risk reduced in later stages after vaccination roll-out. We aimed to assess all-cause and cause-specific mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection in people with or without SMI across pandemic stages, using whole-country data, while accounting for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. METHODS: In this retrospective, whole-country cohort study, we analysed linked electronic health records for all people in England registered to primary care who were alive in November, 2019 (>99% of the population). The study population included people who had COVID-19 between Jan 31, 2020, and June 30, 2023, with information on deaths and vaccination. Data extracted from the NHS England Secure Data Environment provided through the British Heart Foundation Data Science Centre CVD-COVID-UK-COVID-IMPACT Consortium linked datasets were curated to form a dataset in July, 2024. Cox regression estimated differences in all-cause and COVID-19 mortality. Analyses were stratified by pandemic stages, defined by WHO policy and UK Government vaccination roll-out: Jan 31-Sept 30, 2020 (stage 1); Oct 1, 2020-July 18, 2021 (stage 2, vaccination roll-out); and July 19, 2021-June 30, 2023 (stage 3, post-vaccination roll-out). SMI comprised schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or other affective and non-affective disorder with psychosis. A patient and public involvement panel was consulted during design phases of the study. FINDINGS: 13 463 945 people with COVID-19 were identified, of whom 160 190 (1·19%) had SMI. People with SMI were older [mean age [SD], SMI 49·7 years [17·9], non-SMI 45·0 years [17·6]), had a similar sex split (females SMI vs non-SMI: 56·3% vs 56·6%); and were mostly White British (77·3% or 76·3%). People with SMI had higher all-cause mortality than those without (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1·56, 95% CI 1·53-1·59). All-cause mortality risk in people with SMI was elevated in stage 1 (aHR 1·27, 95% CI 1·22-1·32), but larger in the stage 2 (aHR 1·56, 1·51-1·61) and stage 3 (aHR 1·55, 1·50-1·59). Vaccination prevalence was initially higher for people with SMI (in stage 2: 112 795 [73·2%, 95% CI 72·9-73·4], compared with people without SMI, 8 852 970 [67·4%, 67·3-67·4]). By study end, fewer people with SMI were fully vaccinated (127 145 [79·4%, 79·2-79·6]), compared with people without SMI (11 605 915 [87·2%, 87·2-87·3]. Higher COVID-19 mortality risk in people with SMI persisted but was partially attenuated by vaccination (aHR 1·25, 1·17-1·34). INTERPRETATION: Excess mortality in people with SMI persisted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Preventive public health and clinical strategies are needed to address excess mortality and lower vaccination. FUNDING: Health Foundation-Academy of Medical Sciences.

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 需要采取预防性公共卫生和临床策略,以应对患有严重精神疾病(SMI)人群中 死亡率 的过度发生并降低 疫苗接种 发生率。研究结果凸显了针对该脆弱人群采取有针对性干预措施以减少 死亡率 风险的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于关联性电子健康记录,可能在数据完整性和准确性方面存在局限性。由于回顾性研究的性质及潜在未测量混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein (MOG) Antibody-Associated Disease Presenting as Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis Following COVID-19 mRNA Vaccination
papers.abstract: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) is a rapidly progressive autoimmune demyelinating condition that primarily affects the central nervous system. The exact pathogenesis is not well understood, but current literature suggests roles for both environmental triggers and genetic predispositions. Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is an increasingly recognized autoimmune demyelinating disorder that can present with an ADEM-like phenotype, particularly in adults. We report the case of a 53-year-old Asian-American female patient of Taiwanese ancestry with a past medical history of obstructive sleep apnea and no prior autoimmune disease or family history of demyelinating disorders who presented to the emergency room (ER) with left-sided numbness and weakness, ataxia, vertigo, and slurred speech in the context of a three-month long history of headaches that started one day after she received her first dose of Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine. Brain imaging studies showed findings most suggestive of ADEM. Initial pre-treatment cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed markedly elevated protein (473 mg/dL, reference 15-45 mg/dL) with a normal glucose level and mild pleocytosis (6 WBC/μL). Extensive workup was negative for infectious, oncologic, and autoimmune etiologies including negative serum and CSF anti-MOG antibody testing during the acute presentation. The initial treatment of a five-day intravenous methylprednisolone course (250 mg every six hours, total 1,000 mg/day) did not result in significant clinical improvement. The patient was then started on plasma exchange therapy and successfully recovered by the end of the last session with objective improvement in ambulation, dysarthria, and limb strength. The patient tested positive for anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody in serum six months after hospital discharge at a titer of 1:32 by live cell-based assay. This case provides an example of a rare but serious event temporally associated with the SARS-CoV-19 mRNA vaccine and MOGAD presenting as ADEM in a previously healthy adult. The absolute risk of demyelinating events following COVID-19 vaccination is extremely low, and the benefit of vaccination vastly outweighs these rare risks.
